source_title: osolmaz/switch: A framework for building decision-model harnesses for any kind of task. Your program offers the model a short list of next steps, and the model picks one at a time until it can answer. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
switch is a harness framework for decision models like Jev. It gives a decision model an agent loop for finite choices. Your code turns the state of a task into typed questions, such as which next step to take from a short list, and the model picks the answers.
A simple explainer for switch, also on YouTube
A decision model answers typed questions with probabilities and writes no text, so it cannot generate the tool calls that a coding agent harness such as Pi relies on. switch generates the tool calls for it in code, and the model only picks one from that finite set. TypeSafe calls these models System One models , and its Jev was the first; llama.cpp serves open ones through the same API.
switch puts what many people already write by hand, a decision-model API called over several steps, behind one abstract interface. You implement a domain, which defines the state of a task and the functions that turn a state into the model's questions and its answers into the next state. Chess is a domain, and so is a rubric judge for evals.
A main use is a judge in an eval. At the end of a task run that involves many documents, the usual judge extracts the text of the PDF, Word and Markdown files and puts all of it into the context. When the visual formatting of the output is a criterion, every page has to go in as an image too. With 200 pages and a question that needs only a few of them, most of that context is wasted. With switch, the decision model navigates the documents and takes in only what it needs. The rubric judge works this way. It reads parts of files, looks at page images and searches for terms, one step at a time, until it can grade each rubric item.
switch works with any decision model that pi-ai lists as a classifier, Jev among them, as docs/DECISION_MODEL_API.md explains. Jev itself is weak at chess, and as a judge it is not yet good enough to replace the strongest chat models. Once a better model has generated enough data, an open decision model can be fine-tuned on one domain. Trained in a harness like switch's, it should do that job both better and more cheaply. A narrow domain leaves a lot to gain, since an agent built for one specific job could cost a hundredth of what a general model costs.
Domain: your code for one kind of task, such as chess or routing a support ticket. It gives each case as a state machine.
Case: one task of a domain, such as one game, loaded from a case folder.
State: JSON with everything the domain needs to know about where a case is.
Question function: gives the questions that the model must answer in a state. When it gives none, the run ends.
Question and answer: a bool , choice or score question, by id. Every answer comes with the model's probabilities.
Pick: a choice question whose answers are the state's choices , such as the legal moves. The picking helper builds it from a list of choices.
Transition function: gives the next state from a state and the model's answers.
View function: optional. Turns a state into what the model reads, within a token budget.
Step: one round of questions, answers and transition.
Outcome: optional. How a case ended in the domain's terms, such as "white wins".
Trace: every state, question and answer of a run, in one file. A replay reads it and asks no model.
Harness: a program that runs a domain on case folders, with switch's run and replay commands.
The domain makes the case's initial state.
The question function gives the state's questions. If there are none, the run ends.
The model reads the view of the state and answers every question.
The transition function makes the next state from the answers, and the run goes back to step 2.
A run also ends when a request fails, or at a step limit that a domain may set as a safety net. docs/MATH.md writes the loop down in symbols.

Rubric judge grades a saved answer to a task against the task's rubric.
Chess plays chess against random moves, Stockfish, or itself.
WikiRace races from one Wikipedia article to another by following links.
A domain gives initial , questions and transition , and optionally view . This one routes a support ticket. The model reads logs one at a time until it picks stop, and then a last step asks which team gets the ticket.
Run it with any classifier model that pi-ai lists. pi-ai finds the key in the environment, such as TYPESAFE_API_KEY :
docs/DOMAINS.md has the rules of picks, stop choices, views, limits and choice types.
A harness turns a domain into a program that runs case folders. Its setup returns a runner:
commandLine makes it a program with run and replay . It is a Commander program, so the harness can add commands of its own:
docs/DOMAINS.md covers definitions, a domain's own flags and API keys.
run writes a run folder with each case's result, trace and requests. A stopped run goes on where it stopped.
view plays a run back in the browser, step by step, and follows cases live. It is the viewer , a separate package in this repository that the examples add.
replay runs a case again from its trace without the model. With --fork , it repeats the first n steps and lets a model go on from there.
docs/DOMAINS.md says when a replay fails and what a run folder holds.
